name: E0_2_mismatch_drift_coupling
title: Magnitude probe: does PCM drift re-expose the transistor mismatch that threshold verification absorbed, under global drift compensation, and which compensation node avoids it?
hypothesis: In a 6T2M analog CAM the bound is V_TH + G (V_SL/V_TX - 1)/beta: a non-drifting additive transistor term plus a drifting PCM term. Verifying the threshold through the search path absorbs each cell's mismatch into G. When PCM drift is compensated globally at the input DAC, the absorbed V_TH mismatch reappears as (1/a - 1) dV_TH; compensating at the divider supply leaves only a V_TX-dependent term; a mismatch-invariant global scaling of G leaves none. A crossbar MAC array does not have this coupling because its offsets can be corrected per column at the output.

pcm_model.source: AIHWKit PCMLikeNoiseModel (IBM/aihwkit master, read 2026-10-12); Nandakumar et al., ICECS 2019, IEEE Xplore 8964852

cell_model.source: C. Li et al., Nat. Commun. 11, 1638 (2020), Eq. 1 (6T2M analog CAM, divider transistor in the triode regime)
cell_model.equation: V_bound = V_TH + G (V_SL / V_TX - 1) / beta; V_TX is the match-line pull-down threshold for the lower bound and the inverter threshold for the upper bound
cell_model.v_th_source: assumption: lower end of the 0.2-0.6 V data-line range Li 2020 uses for 4-bit discrimination
cell_model.v_tx_source: assumption: must lie below V_SL; gives c_nom = V_SL/V_TX - 1 = 0.4286
cell_model.mapping_source: assumption: the normalized threshold range [0, 1] is mapped onto 2.5-22.5 uS, leaving 2.5 uS headroom at both ends of the AIHWKit 0-25 uS range so that threshold verification can absorb offsets
cell_model.beta_rule: beta_nom = c_nom (g_hi - g_lo) / r_in, so k_nom = r_in / (g_hi - g_lo)

mismatch.source: Pelgrom scaling sigma(V_T) = A_VT / sqrt(W L). P. Kinget, device-mismatch chapter (www.ee.columbia.edu/~kinget/papers_files/chapter3.pdf): A_VT0 ~ 0.5 mV.um per nm of t_ox + 3.4 mV.um. Assumptions: a 130-nm-class 1.8-V device with t_ox ~ 4 nm (A_VT ~ 5.4 mV.um) and W x L = 0.42 um x 0.15 um give sigma(V_T) ~ 22 mV; 20 mV is taken as the primary value. The beta mismatch value is an assumption.
mismatch.draws: per (dataset, split, device seed) one standard-normal vector of length K for each of dV_TH, dV_TX, d_beta from numpy default_rng([base_seed, ds_idx, split, dev, 2]) in that order; every mismatch setting scales the same draws (paired)

programming.threshold: primary: G is set so that the cell's own bound equals the target at t0 (absorbs the mismatch); clipped to [0, g_max]; then AIHWKit programming noise is added to G
programming.conductance: secondary (m20 only): G is set to the nominal value g_lo + theta (g_hi - g_lo)

nodes.dac: DAC gain scaled by a_hat around V_TH,nom
nodes.supply: divider supply V_SL(t) = V_TX,nom (1 + c_nom / a_hat)
nodes.ideal: G -> G / a_hat inside the bound (mismatch-invariant reference)

replica: a_hat(t) = mean of 64 replica PCM cells programmed to 12.5 uS at t / their mean right after programming (as E0.1); a_hat = 1 in the prog condition

datasets.synthetic: sklearn make_classification(n_samples=5000, n_features=20, n_informative=10, n_redundant=4, n_classes=4, n_clusters_per_class=2, class_sep=1.0, random_state=20261012)

model: sklearn RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=16, max_depth=6, random_state=split_seed); stratified 70/30 split with random_state=split_seed; identical to E0.1
pcm_draws: make_draws([base_seed, ds_idx, split, dev], K, 5, 64) exactly as E0.1; one device per bound (column 0)

metrics.acc_ref: accuracy of the ideal 4-bit quantized CAM (no device noise, no mismatch), as E0.1
metrics.loss: acc_ref - accuracy in percentage points, averaged over 3 splits x 5 device seeds per dataset
metrics.mean_loss: mean of the per-dataset losses over the 5 datasets
metrics.conditions: prog: programming noise and mismatch at t0 (a_hat = 1, all nodes identical); all@t: programming noise, drift and accumulated read noise at t

decision.primary: mismatch setting m20, threshold programming, 4 bits
decision.gate_A: PASS (the coupling is first-order) if mean_loss(dac, all@365d) - mean_loss(ideal, all@365d) >= 1.0 pp
decision.classification: if gate A passes: GO_STRONG if mean_loss(supply, all@365d) - mean_loss(ideal, all@365d) >= 1.0 pp (no conventional global node is mismatch-invariant; a new compensation circuit is needed); otherwise GO_WEAK (compensating at the divider supply already avoids the coupling)
decision.secondary: 30-day differences, the other mismatch settings, conductance programming, clipping counts and path integrity are reported only

checks.check_2_nominal_mapping_exact: zero mismatch, no PCM noise or drift: effective theta equals the quantized theta for every node and both programming modes (1e-12)
checks.check_3_nodes_equal_without_mismatch: zero mismatch with the full PCM model: dac, supply and ideal give identical effective thresholds at every time (1e-12)
checks.check_4_closed_forms_uniform_drift: uniform drift (nu_mean_a = 0 so mu_nu = 0.049 for every state, sigma_nu = 0, no programming or read noise), m20 mismatch, threshold programming: the implemented effective thresholds of none, dac, supply and ideal equal the hand-derived closed forms for unclipped cells at every time (1e-12)

not_modelled: PCM current-voltage nonlinearity (matters for the supply node, which raises the voltage across the PCM over time)
transistor operation outside the triode regime at low conductance (Li 2020 notes the linear relation fails there)
temperature dependence of PCM conductance, drift and transistor thresholds
match-line sensing errors and timing; input DAC quantization
